gaps.sentence: I'll never forget the day ___ we first met.
gaps.explanation: 'When' replaces 'on which' after time nouns like day, year and moment.

gaps.sentence: This is the worst storm ___ we have had for years.
gaps.hint: after a superlative ('the worst'), use this pronoun
gaps.explanation: 'That' follows superlatives in defining relative clauses; 'which' is considered poor style there.

gaps.sentence: The chair on ___ the cat was sleeping was my grandmother's.
gaps.explanation: 'On which' is the formal pattern for things; 'on where' and 'on that' are not grammatical.

gaps.sentence: Pablo, ___ speaks five languages, works as an interpreter.
gaps.explanation: Non-defining clauses about people take 'who'; 'that' never follows a comma in standard English.

gaps.sentence: The committee rejected a plan ___ costs had been underestimated.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose costs' means 'the plan's costs'; 'which' would need 'the costs of which'.

gaps.sentence: The programme ___ I watched last night was about volcanoes.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to things, even when it is the object of the clause.

gaps.sentence: She was two hours late, ___ annoyed the interviewer.
gaps.hint: comment on the whole situation before the comma
gaps.explanation: When a clause comments on the whole previous statement, use 'which' after the comma.

gaps.sentence: It was the best meal ___ I have ever eaten.
gaps.hint: after a superlative, this pronoun is preferred
gaps.explanation: After superlatives ('the best ...'), 'that' is the preferred relative pronoun in defining clauses.
